# stlink-tools

**Flash and debug STM32 targets through an ST-Link probe**

- **Version recorded:** 1.8.0
- **Categories:** `programmer`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/stlink-org/stlink>

## What it does

Four programs for ST-Link probes: `st-flash` writes and reads flash, `st- info` identifies the probe and target, `st-util` provides a GDB server, and `st-trace` reads the SWO trace pin.

## Why you would want it

ST-Link probes are on the front of every Nucleo and Discovery board and cost a few pounds standalone, which makes them the default way onto an STM32. This is the lighter alternative to openocd for that one family — fewer configuration files and a faster path to a working flash command.

## Before it will work

An ST-Link probe. Access comes from the `programmer` hardware class; the package ships rules for 11 identifiers covering the V1 through V3 probes.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`electronics`](../profiles/electronics.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install stlink-tools --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `st-info-probe`.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `stlink-tools`

## Known problems

A cloned ST-Link with mismatched firmware reports a target it cannot then talk to, which reads as a broken board rather than a broken probe. `st-info --probe` is the first thing to run and it distinguishes the two.

    STM32 devices in DFU mode present `0483:df11`, the generic STM32
bootloader identifier this catalog refuses to treat as a device — that is dfu-util's job, not this package's.
